scenes.title: Tabletop Sally-Anne puppet stage as Anne moves the glass marble from the round wicker basket into the closed rectangular box
scenes.era: 1985, MRC Cognitive Development Unit testing table, London

layout.description: Sunlit 1985 London developmental playroom with a clean wooden child-height table holding two small cloth-dressed dolls (Sally and Anne), one round woven wicker basket with a lid on the left, one crisp white rectangular cardboard box with a lid on the right, and a gleaming blue-swirl glass marble.

positions.where: seated across the low wooden table moving Doll Anne's hands to transfer the glass marble from the round wicker basket into the rectangular box while Doll Sally rests out of sight below the table edge
watching intently across the table, then pointing one clear index finger back to Sally's round wicker basket when Sally returns

props.name: round woven wicker basket (Sally's)
props.period_detail: small lidded tan basket on the left side of the table — empty after the secret swap
props.physical_behavior: correctly pointed to by 4.5-year-olds answering 'Where will Sally LOOK?'

props.name: rectangular lidded box (Anne's) & glass marble
props.period_detail: crisp white lidded box on the right holding the secretly transferred blue glass marble
props.physical_behavior: pointed to by 3-year-olds swayed by reality bias

props.name: two small cloth-dressed tabletop dolls (Sally & Anne)
props.period_detail: simple matte-porcelain/cloth study puppets in red vs blue aprons
props.physical_behavior: stage the exit, secret transfer, and return cleanly

actions.verb_sequence: places the glass marble into the round wicker basket and exits below the table rim -> Doll Anne lifts the marble across into the rectangular box and closes both lids
Researcher asks 'Where will Sally look?' -> 4-year-old Child mannequin points steadily to the round wicker basket

reactions.reaction: smiles knowingly, holding BOTH facts cleanly: marble is in the box, yet Sally believes basket
checks off all three items: Belief Question + Reality Control + Memory Control

scenes.wardrobe: 1985 British developmental lab attire: warm wool cardigan over collared shirt on researcher; corduroy pinafore/jumper over striped tee on child.
scenes.lighting: Warm high-key London window daylight across natural wood, wicker basket, and white box.
scenes.recognition_hook: You just watched Anne hide the marble in the white box — yet predicting Sally will still check her empty wicker basket requires holding two conflicting worlds inside one head.

key_visual.description: a 1985 tabletop developmental test with two small dolls, a round lidded wicker basket, a rectangular lidded white box, and a glass marble as a child points to the basket

layout.description: Side-by-side tabletop moment comparing a 3-year-old pointing eagerly to the white box (where the marble really sits) vs a 4.5-year-old pointing to the wicker basket.

positions.where: pointing straight at Anne's rectangular box despite passing both memory controls

scenes.title: Modern Double Empathy & Adult 'Tap-the-Song' Curse of Knowledge

layout.description: Bright seminar table where one adult taps knuckles rhythmically on oak expecting the listener across the table to recognize 'Happy Birthday' — while the listener hears only random knocks.

positions.where: tapping desk rhythmically confident the melody is obvious
tilting head puzzled hearing disconnected wooden taps

props.period_detail: Elizabeth Newton's classic adult Curse of Knowledge score
props.physical_behavior: proves healthy adults make Sally-Anne errors daily

actions.verb_sequence: taps song -> Listener guesses wrong -> Tapper laughs realizing the orchestra only played inside their own head

reactions.reaction: bridge the two-way perspective gap by naming the context aloud

scenes.recognition_hook: Adults guess listeners hear a tapped song 50% of the time — actual score is 2.5%, proving Sally-Anne blind spots never fully retire.
